concept.title: Securing a published site
concept.shortdesc: Generated sites are static and self-contained. This topic says what the plugin guarantees, which headers to set on the host, what authors can introduce and how the build reports it, and where responsibility sits.

conbody.p: securityContent-Security-Policyhosting headersA site built with the plugin is a folder of HTML, CSS, JavaScript and images. There is no server-side code, no login, no cookie, no analytics, and nothing that talks to another origin while a reader is on the page. That makes the security work small and mostly the host's: serve the folder over HTTPS with a handful of headers, and keep an eye on what authors put in diagrams, embeds and links.

ul.li: Same origin only, in every branding mode. Logos are inline SVG or files copied into the site; the fonts that official and NHS modes name are root-relative paths served by the host; the crown crest is suppressed rather than fetched. Continuous integration asserts that no page or stylesheet in any mode references another origin.

One inline script. The only script written into a page is the Design System's own body-class snippet, byte for byte, so its published hash applies; everything else — navigation, search, govuk-frontend initialisation — is a file under govuk/.

li.b: No cookies, no third-party requests, no restricted assets bundled.

ul.li: Valid, accessible output, checked on every build with the Nu HTML checker and axe-core at WCAG 2.2 AA.

section.title: Headers to set on the host
section.p: Where you control response headers, set these. The values below are the ones the plugin's pages are known to satisfy; they are also what govuk.csp=meta writes into each page for hosts that cannot set headers (see ), except that frame-ancestors only works as a header.

entry.p: The hash is the Design System's published value for its body-class snippet. 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is needed only when search is enabled (Pagefind runs its index as WebAssembly); drop it otherwise. style-src 'unsafe-inline' covers the style attributes DITA @style, DITAVAL flags and inlined SVG produce. If you serve GDS Transport or another font from a different origin, add that origin to font-src; do the same for images hosted elsewhere in img-src, or better, host them with the site.

row.entry: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains — once the whole host is on HTTPS.
camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() — the site uses none of these.

section.p: Check the result in a browser's developer tools: with the policy in force there should be no violation reports on any page, including a search. The plugin's repository runs that check on every build against the policy it emits.

section.title: What authors can introduce, and how the build reports it
section.p: DITA content can carry things a static site should not: scripts and event handlers inside an SVG diagram, links whose scheme runs code, images or objects fetched from another origin (which breaks the same-origin guarantee and reveals readers' addresses to a third party), and embeds of arbitrary types. The toolkit renders them as authored; the plugin makes them visible and gives the publisher the choice. Every finding is a build warning, never an error — a publisher's build always completes.

ul.li: Inlined SVG diagrams are sanitised by default (govuk.svg.sanitize; GOVK004W names what was found and whether it was removed).
Diagrams and MathML are inlined only from under the input directory (govuk.inline.scope; GOVK005W).

Remote images and SVG references, object embeds and script-scheme links are reported per occurrence (GOVK006W) and rendered as authored under govuk.content.policy=warn, or replaced by a marked placeholder under strip; govuk.content.warnings=no silences the report.
With a Content-Security-Policy in force, content it would block is reported (GOVK007W) so it can be fixed before readers see a broken image.

section.p: Every code is explained in ; the parameters are in .

ul.li: Keep diagrams static. No script, no event-handler attributes, no foreignObject; link with ordinary https: or relative targets; reference only files that travel with the publication. See for what inlining preserves.
Host what you show. Images, objects and fonts belong in the publication, not on another server. A remote image is reported on every build and blocked by the recommended policy.
Links point at pages, not code. A javascript: target is reported and may be stripped. External links open in a new tab with rel="noopener", as the toolkit renders them.
Embeds are a last resort. An object is reported whenever it appears; prefer an image, a figure or a link.

section.title: Where responsibility sits
section.p: The plugin answers for its stylesheets, build logic, CSS and JavaScript, and for the sites and print documents they produce. It does not answer for DITA-OT's XML parsing, DTD and catalog resolution or key and chunk processing, for govuk-frontend, for Pagefind, or for the host's configuration. To report a vulnerability in the plugin, use the repository's private reporting form — see — rather than a public issue.
